ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), as amended; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2011; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Exemptions and Applications) Regulations 2010; Companies Act 1993 and Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994; New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020; Terrorism Suppression Act 2002; Income Tax Act 2007 for tax-transparency and CRS beneficial-ownership records.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (no freely accessible central public UBO register is maintained; AML/CFT reporting entities and New Zealand company service providers must collect and retain accurate beneficial-ownership information and produce it to the Financial Markets Authority, Reserve Bank of New Zealand, Department of Internal Affairs, and law-enforcement authorities on request; nominee shareholders are not prohibited but must disclose nominee status and the look-through analysis must identify every natural person holding 25% or more of the shares or voting rights)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copy of the passport page of each proposed shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority in the individual's country of nationality, with notarization by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; for non-Hague Convention countries, full consular legalization by the nearest New Zealand embassy, high commission, or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency for each corporate shareholder or corporate ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registered agent in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; if issued by a registered agent, the certificate must be notarized and then apostilled or legalized through the same authentication chain

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English translation of all non-English corporate, identity, and source-of-funds documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand-accredited translator or court-certified translator in the issuing jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translation certificate notarized and covered by the same Hague Apostille or consular legalization cycle as the underlying source document

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for each shareholder contributing capital or purchasing the company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or financial institution maintaining the shareholder's or ultimate beneficial owner's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer signature authenticated by notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization when required by the New Zealand reporting entity's enhanced due diligence policy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / no-criminal-conviction certificate for each proposed director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal-record authority or national police service of the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; for non-Hague states, authentication by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and legalization by a New Zealand consular officer

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening standards: all proposed directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and beneficial owners of any corporate shareholder, as well as the intended LME warrant and documentary-credit counterparties, must be screened before incorporation and continuously thereafter against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, the UK sanctions list where relevant, New Zealand sanctions designations maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade under the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020, the New Zealand Police designated-terrorist list under the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002, and the FMA, DIA, and RBNZ AML/CFT advisories. Positive matches require refusal or enhanced due diligence with senior-management approval. For all domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their immediate family members and known close associates, enhanced due diligence must include source of wealth, source of funds, transaction monitoring, and periodic re-screening. The screening tool must include adverse-media and enforcement-action checks; results must be retained in the AML/CFT compliance register.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register, Name Reservation Portal (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz; company name availability search and reservation through the NZ Companies Register)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory filing language is English. Company names must be expressed in Latin-alphabet characters. Te reo Maori names are accepted, including Maori macron diacritics. Non-Latin scripts such as Chinese characters, Cyrillic, Greek, and Arabic are not accepted as the registered name; a Latin-alphabet transliteration and certified English translation must be provided. The name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' unless a statutory exemption applies; internet-style endings such as '.com', '.nz', '.limited' are not permitted as company-name suffixes. The Registrar will refuse a name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or a name that is offensive or likely to mislead under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No. 105), notably sections 10 (registration of companies), 12 (formation of company), 14 (certificate of incorporation), 19 (registered office), 21–23 (company name requirements and reservation), 35–45 (share capital and allotment), 91–92 (constitution of board and first directors), 158 (consent to act as director), and 184 (written resolutions); supplemented by the Companies (Fees) Regulations 2023 and read together with the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for the company's financial reporting duties. The entity is organised as a private company with an 'International Company' designation for the offshore-origin trading vehicle; the Companies Act 1993 applies as the sole national incorporation statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — operating through the New Zealand Companies Register online portal at www.companies-register.govt.nz.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic Incorporation Application (Companies Register digital form; the statutory 'application for registration' under section 10 of the Companies Act 1993) filed through the New Zealand Companies Register online portal; a PDF constitution may be uploaded as an annex if the default rules in Schedule 2 of the Act are not adopted.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up share capital and no escrow or banked deposit rule under the Companies Act 1993. The company may be incorporated with a single no-par value share or multiple shares; shares may be fully or partly paid. Each founding subscriber must subscribe for at least one share at an issue price determined by the board, with the issue proceeds payable to the company in accordance with sections 35–45 of the Act. For this International Company vehicle, the authorised capital is set at 1,000 ordinary shares of no par value, fully paid at NZD 1.00 per share, with no requirement to deposit capital into a designated escrow account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company') — Adopted by written resolution of the initial directors on [Date] pursuant to section 184 of the Companies Act 1993, effective upon incorporation.

RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION — That the allotment and issue of 1,000 ordinary shares of no par value to the founding shareholders named in the incorporation application, at an aggregate subscription consideration of NZD 1,000.00, be and is hereby acknowledged, ratified and confirmed, and that the directors be and are hereby authorised to issue share certificates and to record the allotments in the Share Register. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE — That the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed and adopted at [Registered Office Address, New Zealand], and that the Registrar of Companies be notified of such registered office in compliance with section 19 of the Companies Act 1993. 3. FIRST DIRECTORS AND OFFICER APPOINTMENTS — That [Full Name 1] be and is hereby appointed Director and Managing Director; [Full Name 2] be and is hereby appointed Director and Chief Financial Officer; and [Full Name 3] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary, each to hold office until successors are duly appointed. Each such officer is authorised, whether alone within delegated limits or jointly, to: (a) open, operate and close bank accounts of the Company; (b) accept, deliver and transfer London Metal Exchange (LME) warrant certificates and instruct LME warrant transfers; (c) execute, endorse and authenticate documentary letters of credit and trade finance documents; and (d) sign all statutory returns, contracts, invoices and operational documents of the Company. 4. BANKING AUTHORITY — That the principal bank account be established with [Bank Name] in New Zealand, and that the banking mandates, signatory lists and corresponding schedules be executed in the form required by such bank. 5. CONSTITUTION AND SEAL — That the Constitution delivered with the incorporation application (or, if none, the default rules in Schedule 2 of the Companies Act 1993) be and is hereby adopted as the governing instrument of the Company, and that the common seal, if any, be kept at the registered office.

DATED this ____ day of ______________, 202__. ______________________________________ [Full Name 1], Managing Director

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register online portal (www.companies-register.govt.nz), Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name availability search against the New Zealand Companies Register to verify that the proposed company name is not identical or almost identical to a name already reserved or registered, and does not contain a restricted or prohibited word under sections 21–22 of the Companies Act 1993. If the name is available, the applicant may either reserve the name for 20 working days (fee NZD 10, approximately USD 6) or proceed directly to the electronic incorporation application using the same name. For the 'International Company' designation, advise the Registrar that the company is a licensed international trading vehicle; the word 'International' is permissible in a company name without further consent, whereas words such as 'Bank' or 'Trust' would require approval of the relevant sectoral regulator, which is not applicable here.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name
Name availability search result printed from the Companies Register
Consent letter of any restricted-word approver (if applicable; not applicable for this entity)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses the name under section 21, the applicant will receive a written notice of refusal; the remedy is to re-lodge the incorporation application with a revised name that is no longer identical or almost identical to an existing register entry. Refused-name fees are not refunded but may be credited toward the subsequent application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal counsel / licensed incorporation agent (preparation); no government filing at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the founding shareholders elect to contract out of the default rules in Schedule 2 of the Companies Act 1993, settle and execute a bespoke Constitution addressing share transfer pre-emptions, director powers, indemnity, and decision-making thresholds. Otherwise, adopt the statutory default rules by written election in the incorporation application. Prepare the full legal name, date of birth, residential address and share subscription of each founding shareholder and each initial director. Obtain each director's signed consent to act under section 158 of the Companies Act 1993. Confirm the registered office will be a physical address in New Zealand or the office of a licensed registered-office service provider.
required_dossiers: Constitution (PDF) or written election to adopt Schedule 2 default rules
Director consent to act forms (section 158)
Share subscription schedule showing classes, number of shares, issue price, and amount paid or credited as paid
Copy of passport / national ID for each director and beneficial owner (for AML/CFT onboarding)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed director is disqualified (minor, undischarged bankrupt, or prohibited under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993), replace the director before filing and execute a fresh consent form; no adverse action arises from the internal preparation step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register electronic incorporation service (www.companies-register.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Register and select 'Incorporate a Company'. Enter the approved company name, company type (private company), registered office address, address for service in New Zealand, election regarding constitution, full particulars of directors and shareholders, share allotment and deemed paid-up amount, and business activity descriptor (ISIC 4662 — wholesale of metals and metal ores, copper cathodes trading). Upload the adopted constitution, if any. Pay the incorporation fee of NZD 150.00 (approximately USD 90) by debit or credit card. Each director must complete the integrated electronic consent; the system will generate the application record for the Registrar's determination.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic incorporation application
Electronic director consent consents as embedded in the filing
Constitution PDF (if adopted)
Proof of payment of the NZD 150.00 filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or rejection notice, the applicant may amend the application and re-submit it through the same portal within 20 working days without paying a second fee if the issue is cured; if the name itself is invalid, file a fresh application with a corrected name and pay the applicable fee. Escalate unresolved queries to the Companies Office Contact Centre for administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (system-generated issuance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Registrar issues an electronic Certificate of Incorporation under section 14 of the Companies Act 1993, which evidences the legal existence of the company from the date of incorporation. The system simultaneously issues the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), which is the national identifier for all government and trading interactions. Download the certificate and the company extract from the Companies Register, verify the company name, company number, officers, issued shares, and registered office, and retain these documents as the foundational legal record for all subsequent bank, tax, and trading counterparty onboarding.
required_dossiers: Electronic Certificate of Incorporation (PDF)
NZBN auto-issuance confirmation
Certified company extract from the New Zealand Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error (wrong company number, name or date), file a 'Company Update' through the Companies Register to correct the underlying register data; the Registrar will re-issue a corrected certificate within one working day at no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration for IRD Number, GST and Income Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand — myIR SecureOnline platform (www.ird.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NZBN and Certificate of Incorporation, register the company with Inland Revenue for income tax. Apply for a Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration, which is mandatory once annual supplies exceed NZD 60,000; because copper cathode trading typically generates turnover above this threshold, GST registration at 15% is recommended from the effective date of the first taxable supply. If the company will employ staff, also register for PAYE and payday filing. All applications are submitted electronically through myIR with the company's NZBN as the primary authentication key.
required_dossiers: NZBN and Certificate of Incorporation
Registered office address and New Zealand address for service
Director and shareholder identification details
Company bank account details for GST refunds and tax payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue queries the application, respond through myIR with the requested identification or address evidence within the stated deadline; a GST registration, once issued, may be backdated to the earlier of the date of application or the first taxable supply, thereby preserving the correct tax point for LC settlements and LME invoicing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Statutory Registers and Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company (private law requirement; no government filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or pass a written resolution under section 184 of the Companies Act 1993) and adopt the Pro Forma First Board Resolution set out in the incorporation dossier: ratify the issue of shares, adopt the registered office, appoint the Managing Director, Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary, and authorise the banking mandate and trade-signing authority for LME warrant transfers and documentary letter of credit operations. Open the statutory registers required by sections 87, 90 and 140 of the Act — the Share Register, Directors' Register, and Interests Register — and execute and issue share certificates to each shareholder.
required_dossiers: Signed First Board Resolution or written resolution
Share certificates issued to founding shareholders
Share Register, Directors' Register and Interests Register
Minutes of the first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any appointment must be amended, the board may pass a subsequent resolution; provided the amendment does not invalidate the incorporation, the Companies Register is updated online through the 'Officer Details' function, and corrected minutes are appended to the board minute book.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the wholesale trading of Grade A refined copper cathodes under ISIC 4662 does not require an industrial manufacturing licence in New Zealand. The general regulatory counterpart bodies are WorkSafe New Zealand (occupational health and safety oversight under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015), the New Zealand Customs Service (for import/export border control of copper), and the local territorial authority (for commercial building and occupancy compliance where a physical office or warehouse exists); none of these imposes an industrial licence on a pure trading operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no manufacturing, refining, smelting or industrial operating permit is exigible for the contracted scope of physical arbitrage trading of copper cathodes. Should the company later add warehousing or re-packaging, it would require a Building Occupancy/Warrant of Fitness and territorial authority 'Change of Use' consent under the Building Act 2004, but still no separate trading licence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, together with the relevant regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Triggered — an office-based wholesale trading operation is not an activity listed in Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991 as requiring a Full Environmental Impact Assessment; no resource consent, discharge permit, or EPA approval is required at formation. A voluntary environmental certification (e.g., ISO 14001) may be adopted for commercial credibility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at incorporation stage for a non-industrial trading office. If the company subsequently operates an incidental storage or logistics facility for copper cathodes, it must observe: (i) the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality 2004 (for any combustion or particulate sources, otherwise exempt for a storage shed); (ii) the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Sources of Drinking Water) Regulations 2007; (iii) the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 for packaging and off-specification material disposal; and (iv) regional council stormwater discharge permit rules for any outdoor storage to prevent copper-laden run-off above the applicable council threshold.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The company's commercial office premises must hold a current Building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF) where the building systems are subject to annual inspection under the Building Act 2004, together with an approved Fire Evacuation Scheme or Fire Safety Certificate issued under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. As a Person Conducting a Business or Undertaking (PCBU), the company must comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015: document a workplace risk assessment, ensure worker engagement and consultation, and display emergency procedures. WorkSafe New Zealand has unrestricted entry rights to inspect; clearance for the physical premises is confirmed by the building owner's BWoF, a fire compliance statement, and an occupational health and safety policy signed by the Managing Director.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Tāke), New Zealand's national tax authority, operating the myIR Secure Online Services portal (https://myir.ird.govt.nz) and the public IRD website (https://www.ird.govt.nz). Customs and export control administration rests with the New Zealand Customs Service (Ngā Rōpū Tiaki Taonga o Aotearoa) via its Trade Single Window system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain an 8-9 digit New Zealand IRD number. The Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) applies as a non-resident company by submitting the non-resident company IRD number application (through myIR or the applicable IRD non-resident paper forms) together with: (i) certified Cook Islands certificate of incorporation, constitution, and registered agent certificate; (ii) director and ultimate beneficial owner identification; and (iii) contact details including a New Zealand address or NZ-resident agent where a taxable activity is anticipated. Where the entity carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand (e.g., wholesale supplies of copper cathodes), a simultaneous GST registration application must be filed; the same IRD number operates as the GST registration number. For export activities, the entity must additionally register as a client of the New Zealand Customs Service to lodge electronic export declarations through the Trade Single Window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — Territorial_Scope: For New Zealand income tax, the CK_IC is a non-resident foreign company (not incorporated in New Zealand, and lacking New Zealand head office or central management and control) taxed only on New Zealand-sourced income; no pass-through treatment is available. Formation-jurisdiction status: Tax_Exempt_Zone (the Cook Islands International Company is statutorily exempt from Cook Islands income tax under the International Companies Act).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no check-the-box entity classification regime. Statutory elections/mechanisms available: (i) voluntary GST registration below the NZD 60,000 threshold; (ii) look-through company (LTC) election under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 — available only to New Zealand-resident closely held companies, and therefore unavailable to the non-resident CK_IC; (iii) CFC active-business exemption and attributed income elections for New Zealand-resident controllers; (iv) joint related-party election for zero-rating of exported goods where the GST Act conditions are satisfied; and (v) hybrid mismatch rules (Income Tax Act 2007 subpart FH and Tax Administration Act 1994 Part 4B, effective for income years beginning on or after 1 July 2018) which operate by mandatory adjustment with a statutory ordering rule; a taxpayer may seek Commissioner approval to vary the ordering where a foreign hybrid mismatch regime requires a different sequence of adjustments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: New Zealand Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; an invoice-credit value-added tax administered by Inland Revenue and supplemented by border import GST and customs duty collected by the New Zealand Customs Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period (compulsory registration); voluntary registration is available below the threshold for persons carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand. Non-resident suppliers of remote/digital services to New Zealand consumers must register under the offshore supplier rules if their supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous control, or digital tax-stamping mandate applies. GST is return-based: registered persons file periodic returns electronically via myIR and remit net tax. E-invoicing follows the Peppol framework — central government agencies must be able to receive Peppol e-invoices, while B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary. Export declarations, however, must be lodged electronically with the New Zealand Customs Service through the Trade Single Window; no transaction-level API clearance is imposed on GST suppliers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11 of the GST Act 1985, a supply of goods is zero-rated where the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply (or such further period as the Commissioner allows), and where the supplier holds the customary evidence of export. Supplies of goods to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply are also zero-rated if the goods are subsequently exported. For offshore services (including trading, brokerage, or arbitrage support), zero-rating applies where the services are supplied to a non-resident outside New Zealand and are not supplied in connection with New Zealand land, goods situated in New Zealand when the services are performed, or services physically performed in New Zealand. For Grade A copper cathodes, the supplier must be the exporter of record, title must pass to the overseas buyer (e.g., FOB/CIF Incoterms or LME warrant transfer), and the goods must physically leave New Zealand; goods sold on an LME warrant without entering or leaving New Zealand are supplied outside New Zealand and fall outside the New Zealand GST net entirely, meaning no GST output tax is charged and no New Zealand input tax credit is available for related costs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service electronic Export Declaration (Customs export entry lodged via the Trade Single Window) identifying HS code 7403.11.00 (refined copper cathodes), gross weight, value, and overseas destination
Original negotiable Bill of Lading (or Sea Waybill) evidencing shipment from the New Zealand port of loading to the foreign destination port, consigned to the overseas buyer
LME-certified warehouse warrant or quality certificate evidencing Grade A refined copper cathode deliverable status
Commercial invoice and packing list issued by the CK_IC in the name of the exporter
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103 payment confirmation, or documentary-letter-of-credit settlement document evidencing receipt of export proceeds within the repatriation deadline
Evidence of physical export within 28 days of the time of supply (e.g., Customs departure certification, port manifest, container tracking or load-port tally)
Export sale contract or LME sale confirmation incorporating the Incoterms rule and evidencing offshore transfer of title and risk
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: A zero-rating claim that fails the statutory export requirements recharacterises the supply as standard-rated, rendering the supplier liable for 15% GST on the consideration plus use-of-money interest under section 120 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 from the due date of the offending return. Civil shortfall penalties under section 141 of that Act apply at graduated rates: 20% for failure to exercise reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% where evasion or similar offence is established. Retrospective reassessments may be issued within the statutory time bar (generally 4 years, extended in cases of evasion) and GST refunds already paid are clawed back with interest. Dishonest or false export documentation exposes the entity and its officers to prosecution under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 (penalties up to NZD 250,000 per offence and forfeiture of goods) and the Crimes Act 1961 (tax evasion offences carrying imprisonment for natural persons). The Commissioner may also deregister the taxpayer, require security or bond for future registration, and publish penalty determinations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) is the statutory central bank, prudential regulator of registered banks, and overseer of the national wholesale settlement system (ESAS). The Overseas Investment Office (OIO) administers foreign-investment screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005. The New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and the Department of Internal Affairs supervise anti-money-laundering and countering-financing-of-terrorism obligations. Sanctions administration is conducted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. New Zealand has no dedicated foreign-exchange-control ministry and issues no exchange-control permits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is a freely floating currency fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions, and New Zealand satisfies IMF Article VIII obligations. There is no general exchange-control approval, quota, or conversion requirement applicable to a Cook Islands International Company engaged in wholesale copper cathode trading. Inbound equity injections, shareholder loans, intercompany funding, trade settlements, dividend distributions, loan repayments, and profit remittances may be effected freely in any convertible currency. The only consent-based or quantitative gates relevant to a foreign IC are: (i) the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for acquisitions of sensitive land, significant business assets, or fishing quotas, with ordinary wholesale metals trading and working-capital deployment normally beneath the notifiable thresholds; (ii) the Financial Sanctions Act 2019 regime administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; and (iii) New Zealand tax obligations under the Income Tax Act 2007, including non-resident withholding tax on interest and dividends, and the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 for imported services and commission structures. Practical friction is not FX-convertibility but rather bank compliance verification of source of funds, payment purpose, and beneficial ownership.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. New Zealand maintains a fully liberalised capital account and imposes no statutory timeline for surrendering export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation quota. A copper cathode exporter may retain USD receivables indefinitely in onshore or offshore foreign-currency accounts, net them against payable invoices, or convert them into NZD through any registered bank without central-bank approval. The operative obligations are record-keeping and statistical reporting: the collecting bank must capture accurate balance-of-payments purpose categories (for example 'goods — metals and minerals' or 'trade credit') for each cross-border transaction; the exporter must retain underlying invoices, LME warrants, bills of lading, and SWIFT instructions for AML/CFT and Inland Revenue audit purposes; and any foreign funds parked in a bank account must be reconciled in a manner consistent with the stated commercial activity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Demand Account and USD/NZD Multi-Currency Account with Capital Escrow sub-ledger
Operational Account and Trade Finance Facility; Documentary LC desk
Operational Account with Commodity Trade Settlement Line; USD nostro clearing
Operational and Escrow Account; Metals and Minerals Trade Advisory
Standard Business Operational Account; limited documentary commodity trade finance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for offshore digital EMIs and MEDIUM for locally registered non-bank payment providers. New Zealand has no standalone electronic-money-institution licensing regime; non-bank payment service providers must be registered on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR), belong to an approved dispute-resolution scheme, and be reporting entities under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Offshore digital EMIs cannot directly access the New Zealand clearing infrastructure, cannot hold settlement accounts at the Reserve Bank, and cannot participate in ESAS (Exchange Settlement Account System) or the NZ Clear retail clearing network. In practice, an offshore EMI may be used only as a USD payment gateway in front of a New Zealand-licensed sponsor bank that performs the ultimate NZD settlement. The Cook Islands IC should expect significantly slower onboarding, enhanced beneficial-ownership review, and possible rejection where the EMI is incorporated in a low-tax jurisdiction with no demonstrable substance or New Zealand client-facing presence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors of a non-resident Cook Islands International Company are normally required to appear physically, or by bank-approved video conference, at account opening. Under New Zealand banking practice, the 100-point identification verification rule, combined with enhanced due diligence for offshore tax-exempt companies, makes physical attendance by at least one executive director or one senior ultimate beneficial owner effectively mandatory. Banks such as ANZ, ASB, and BNZ may approve remote opening only where the principal is already an existing client, where a New Zealand-licensed lawyer or accountant introduces the transaction, or where all constitutional and identity documents are notarised and apostilled and transmitted through the Cook Islands registered agent. A projected physical presence in Auckland or Christchurch, or the appointment of a local director, materially accelerates the onboarding timeline and reduces the likelihood of a compliance declination.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company (Cook Islands IC) with no local office, no New Zealand director, and tax-exempt status that appears inconsistent with a genuine physical-copper-trading business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation, constitution, and current certificate of good standing from the Cook Islands Registrar; registered-agent confirmation letter; a complete corporate organogram exhibiting the full beneficial-ownership chain through any nominee shareholders; reviewed or audited financial statements evidencing real copper cathode inventory positions, contractual sale/purchase obligations, or LME warrant holdings; a board resolution approving the banking relationship and specifying the exact commercial purpose; an independent New Zealand tax counsel opinion explaining the IC's tax residency profile and the legal basis for its tax-exempt or treaty position; and original LME warrants, supply agreements, and vessel/bill-of-lading documentation evidencing genuine commodity flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholders, trust-protector structures, or trustee arrangements creating opacity around ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete beneficial-ownership declaration identifying each natural person who ultimately owns or controls 25% or more of the International Company; certified passport pages and proof-of-residential-address for every UBO; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds certificates from a licensed accountant, auditor, or wealth manager; the underlying trust deed and protector resolutions where a trust sits above the company; an independent AML due-diligence report prepared by a New Zealand law firm; and a sworn director's statement confirming that no nominee arrangement obscures control over bank accounts or trade proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person (PEP), or adverse media flags arising from copper suppliers, buyers, freight forwarders, or refining counterparties in jurisdictions subject to enhanced monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A comprehensive sanctions-screening clearance report covering all counterparties, payees, and beneficiaries, produced with a licensed screening tool; the underlying copper cathode purchase and sale contracts together with the LME warrant chain demonstrating lawful origin and absence of any restricted-party nexus; customs import/export entry numbers and transport bills of lading; the full Incoterms schedule (CIF/FOB) for each shipment; bank confirmation of accurate payment-purpose coding; and a written compliance attestation signed by the responsible director undertaking continuous screening of all future payees and trade counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: equity injections and shareholder loans should be routed by SWIFT MT103 (or equivalent) to the New Zealand bank's corresponding account in USD, EUR, or NZD, with field 70 (Remittance Information) quoting the IC legal name, the target account number, and the caption 'Capital injection — Cook Islands International Company'. The receiving New Zealand bank must allocate the correct balance-of-payments classification, normally 'direct investment — equity capital inward' for share injections or 'other investment — loan inward' for shareholder debt. The IC must present a board resolution authorising the injection, a written loan agreement where applicable, and source-of-funds documentation for each contributing shareholder. No Reserve Bank permission or OIO consent is required where the capital is deployed as ordinary working capital for wholesale copper cathode trading; however, if the injection includes the acquisition of an existing New Zealand business, significant business assets, or sensitive land, an Overseas Investment Act clearance may be required before funds may be applied. The bank will credit the funds only after sanctions screening and source-of-funds verification are completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers to copper refiners, smelters, freight forwarders, and logistics providers, using the goods-trade purpose code and the relevant invoice or contract number in the narration; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit — MT700 issuance and MT707 amendments under UCP 600 for payable-at-negotiation copper cathode purchases, with transport documents, quality certificates, and LME-brand certificates presented through the New Zealand bank's trade desk; (c) LME warrant transfers processed through LME Clear and the LME's approved warrant registration system, with the underlying Grade A copper cathode lots moved via warrant instruction; and (d) NZD settle-through legs executed over the Reserve Bank's ESAS real-time gross settlement system, with cross-border USD payments cleared through the bank's United States correspondent (for example JPMorgan Chase or BNY Mellon). SWIFT gpi payment tracking should be used for all high-value outbound wires to enable end-to-end traceability. The IC should maintain separate USD and NZD accounts so that FX conversion is explicit and the trade settlement record remains audit-ready.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forward NZD/USD contracts with variable tenors up to 24 months, executed under the bank's ISDA or FX master agreement.
FX swaps and tom-next/spot-next rolling swaps for daily funding and roll management of NZD/USD and NZD/CNH exposures.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps exchanging USD floating (SOFR) for NZD floating (BKBM) to hedge working-capital and borrowing-cost mismatches.
European-style vanilla FX options, including call and put structures, and zero-premium collar/risk-reversal combinations aligned to forecast copper-cathode sale and purchase cycles.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in CNY, INR, and other restricted-convertibility currencies where the copper supply chain involves Chinese or Indian smelters and the underlying currency cannot be delivered freely outside the home market; NZD/USD NDFs are neither necessary nor appropriate because the NZD is fully convertible.
LME Metals forward contracts and commodity swaps as commodity-price overlays, customarily combined with FX forwards to lock the fully landed NZD cost of copper cathode deliveries.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of International Company — declaration of registered office, registered agent, directors, secretary, members and issued share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Financial Supervisory Commission of the Cook Islands (Cook Islands, Realm of New Zealand)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six calendar months after each anniversary of incorporation; no filing with the New Zealand Companies Office is required for this non-resident, tax-exempt International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 20 per month or part-month; persistent default permits the Registrar to serve 30 days' gazetted notice and strike the International Company off the Register; after strike-off, the company's assets vest in the Crown and its contracts become unenforceable

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under the Cook Islands International Companies Act: no statutory audit is required and no financial statements must be filed with the Registrar. An audit becomes necessary only if the company's articles require it or shareholders holding at least 10% of voting rights validly demand one
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB, or Cook Islands-adopted equivalents; voluntarily prepared financial statements, if produced for management or shareholder use, must follow IFRS but need not be lodged publicly

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed Cook Islands registered agent must obtain an annual written confirmation from directors and members identifying every individual with 25% or more direct or indirect ownership or control, or any person otherwise exercising significant control; the confirmation is maintained in the AML/CFT client due diligence file and is available to the Financial Supervisory Commission. No public UBO filing is made in the Cook Islands or New Zealand

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000 - USD 2,500 per annum depending on risk tier and transaction volume
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 6,000 only if voluntarily audited; not a statutory annual requirement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand levies no statutory tax holidays for commercial wholesale trading entities. A resident company is taxed at 28% on worldwide income unless an exclusion applies. The imputation credit system effectively eliminates double taxation of distributed profits. Eligible taxpayers may claim a 15% R&D tax credit, but classic base-metal arbitrage will not qualify absent qualifying R&D. Depreciation and low-value asset deductions are available under the Income Tax Act 2007. The purported 'Tax-Exempt Zone' label attached to an International Company is not a New Zealand domestic tax status; where the central management and control is in NZ, the entity is a NZ tax resident and taxable at 28%, irrespective of the offshore exempt-zone classification.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (subject to 49% shareholder continuity and business continuity rules)
